findings.claim: The bus explosion scene "depicts the violent attack on the Freedom Riders' bus when it arrived in Birmingham, Alabama".
findings.truth: The Greyhound bus was firebombed at Anniston, Alabama on 14 May 1961. The mob slashed its tyres, chased it, and threw a firebomb into it a few miles outside the town. Birmingham is where the riders on the second (Trailways) bus were beaten by Klansmen; no bus was burned there. The lesson's own opening line for the scene is "Next stop, Anniston, Alabama."
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Freedom Riders (bus burned at Anniston; Birmingham = Trailways station beatings); lesson 2 text at timestamp 13:50

findings.claim: Themes list: "Violence — demonstrated by the attack on the Freedom Riders' bus in Birmingham, Alabama".
findings.truth: The same error as F1. The bus attack the play stages happens at Anniston, Alabama.

findings.claim: "They encountered violent racist protests in which some lost their lives and were often arrested or dumped in Ku Klux Klan territories by the police — despite having the backing of the American government."
findings.truth: No Freedom Rider was killed during the 1961 Rides. Riders were badly beaten and more than 300 were jailed. The American government did not back them: the Kennedys condemned the Rides and called for a "cooling off period", and the administration agreed that the federal government would not stop local police arresting riders at the depots.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Freedom Riders ("The Kennedys called for a 'cooling off period' and condemned the Rides"; the deal that the federal government would not intervene to stop arrests)

findings.claim: "30 marks — 20 marks for answering the question and 10 marks for using drama terminology". Repeated as "10 of the 30 marks are for terminology alone" (lesson 1 conclusion) and "specifically for using drama terminology" (lesson 1 exam tip), and in lesson 4 as "10 of your 30 marks come from using drama terminology" and "10 marks are specifically for drama terminology".
findings.truth: In Section B, 20 marks are for analysing and evaluating the work of others, and 10 marks are for knowledge and understanding of how drama and theatre is developed and performed. Terminology is how a student shows that knowledge; terminology on its own scores nothing. The 30-mark total is correct.
findings.evidence: specs/ocr/drama-J316.md section 3a: "Section B: 10 marks are for AO3 and 20 are for AO4"; AO definitions in section 3b

findings.claim: "For Section B of your OCR Drama exam..." and knowledge check 1: "How many marks is Section B of the OCR Drama exam worth?"
findings.truth: House rule: student-facing text never names the exam board.
findings.evidence: CHECK_PROMPT_GENERIC.md, copyright distancing and board-naming rule

findings.claim: "You have 30 minutes to write your response."
findings.truth: No such rule exists. The written paper lasts 1 hour 30 minutes and is worth 80 marks. Students divide the time themselves, so about 30 minutes for this 30-mark section is advice, not a rule.
findings.evidence: specs/ocr/drama-J316.md, assessment overview (80 marks, 1 hour 30 minutes, 40% of the qualification)

findings.claim: Stage positions in the White Shoppers scene contradict each other. The body text says "The White shoppers were positioned upstage right (USR) ... The LWG's mum was positioned upstage left (USL)". The key fact says "The White shoppers staying USL ...". The mark scheme for practice question 2 rewards "the shoppers USL reducing proxemics, and the mum USR".
findings.truth: Two of the three places (the key fact and the mark scheme) put the shoppers USL and the mum USR. The body paragraph has them the other way round, so a student who learns the body text is marked down by this unit's own mark scheme. Options: (a) correct the body paragraph to shoppers USL and mum USR, which matches the other two places — recommended; (b) correct the key fact and the mark scheme instead. Only the recording (timestamp 13:50) settles which is true, so Tom should check it before the swap.
findings.evidence: internal contradiction between lesson 2 content_html and practice_questions[1].marks

findings.claim: "The Little White Girl always remained stage right, reinforcing her kind, questioning nature."
findings.truth: "Always" is false whichever staging is right. Lesson 2 places the LWG on a tall stool centre stage as the focal point of the White Shoppers scene, and says so three times (body text, key fact, knowledge check). Softened to "was usually positioned".
findings.evidence: internal contradiction with lesson 2 content_html and knowledge_checks[4]

findings.claim: "Connor Bull scene", "when Connor Bull abandoned the Freedom Riders", "when Connor Bull drops the Freedom Riders" — three places.
findings.truth: The name is Bull Connor (Theophilus Eugene Connor), Birmingham's Commissioner of Public Safety, who drove the arrested Nashville riders to the Tennessee state line and abandoned them there. Lesson 3 and the props list in lesson 4 already spell it "Bull Connor".
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Freedom Riders ("Connor drove them back up to the Tennessee line and dropped them off")

findings.claim: Diane Nash is defined as "A student who organised and led the second wave of Freedom Riders from Nashville to Birmingham, Alabama" — the same wording in the glossary and a flashcard.
findings.truth: Nash organised and coordinated the second wave from Nashville. She was not on the bus. The body text of the lesson already says "organised a second wave", which is right.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Freedom Riders ("Nash was a Nashville college student and organizer, not a bus rider herself")

findings.claim: Lighting in the White Shoppers scene: the blue is "removed" on the line "Such a beautiful day", then "removed entirely" again when the LWG is introduced.
findings.truth: The two sentences describe the same change twice. It costs no marks but it is confusing to revise from. Tidy it next time the lesson is edited.

findings.claim: "Live theatre" is defined as "A performance watched in person by the audience, as opposed to a recorded or filmed version", while lesson 2 quotes timestamps "in the recorded version".
findings.truth: The definition is correct in general, but for this written component the performance a student writes about may be a recording or a stream of a live performance. Worth saying in class so nobody thinks a recording disqualifies their answer. Not edited, because the definition itself is not wrong.
findings.evidence: specs/ocr/drama-J316.md, Appendix 5e: "the live performance students refer to can include recordings or streams of live performance"

findings.claim: The Little White Girl's costume item is a "headband" in lesson 3 and a "bow" in lesson 4.
findings.truth: One item with two names. Pick one so students name it consistently in an essay.
findings.evidence: internal contradiction between lesson 3 and lesson 4 content_html

summary: Two HIGH factual errors put the bus firebombing in Birmingham instead of Anniston, Alabama, and the unit repeatedly tells students that 10 of the 30 Section B marks are for terminology alone, when they are for knowledge and understanding of drama. Also corrected: an untrue claim that Freedom Riders died and that the US government backed them, the name "Connor Bull" for Bull Connor, the Diane Nash definition, the exam board named in two student-facing places, and an invented 30-minute rule. One ADJUDICATE: the lesson body and its own mark scheme give opposite stage positions for the White shoppers.
